text: ADR-001 is amended, not superseded (DEC-018, DEC-019): booking-api@v1 takes auth-api@v1's bearer token from the in-memory store; sessions are never in PostgreSQL; there is no logout endpoint. Its Consequences make a missing, unknown or expired token one case at every endpoint that takes the token, 401 UNAUTHORIZED, so booking-api@v1's endpoints answer it with the same envelope profile-api gives. ADR-001's affects already names booking-api@v1: its front matter needs governed_by: [ADR-001, ADR-002], or gate C3's forward-reference warning becomes an error once the file exists.

ADR-001 keeps in-memory sessions and client-side sign-out (DEC-018, DEC-019), so its update asks nothing of auth-api@v1's guarantees on a restart or sign-out beyond what they already rest on. If the touch restates the token guarantee ('accepted ... until expiresAt'), a restart ending every token early is existing behavior (ADR-001 Consequences, first bullet), a clarification rather than a new rule. auth-api@v1's front matter already carries governed_by: [ADR-001] (Q-001).

ADR-001's affects now names simple-login (execution plan C-2, DEC-022), so the root header must keep Governed by: [ADR-001] when the touch restates it, or gate C3 errors. The Decisions bullet on ADR-001 (in-memory sessions, 30 minutes, sign-out on the client) stays true under the amendment.

ADR-001 keeps sessions in memory (DEC-018), so simple-login.integration.2's restart stays a valid expired-token stand-in for AC-2.3 and the intake record's 'revisited if ADR-001's update makes sessions survive a restart' does not fire. The PRD v2 Success test that a restart keeps every booking must sign in again after the restart, since the same restart signs every user out (ADR-001 Consequences).

booking-api@v1 is in ADR-002's affects: its front matter needs governed_by: [ADR-001, ADR-002] (and the body's Governed by line), or gate C3 errors once the file exists. ADR-002 fixes for it: every instant, request and response, is a UTC string in toISOString form (2026-11-05T02:00:00.000Z), never a local time or another offset; the rooms-on-a-date query takes the day as two instants and returns each room's bookings overlapping that half-open range, earliest first; each room carries timeZone (IANA) and its office's name; a booking occupies [start, end), so touching bookings do not overlap; start and end must have UTC minutes a multiple of 15 and zero seconds and milliseconds, end after start; 'started' means the backend's clock reads the start or later (refused for booking, and a booking can be cancelled only while the clock is before its start); my bookings are those whose end is after the backend's clock, soonest first; the overlap refusal carries the room's name and the other booking's start and end as instants, so the web app writes AC-5.3's message.

Two choices ADR-002 leaves to the draft. (1) How far ahead: London's clock changes are 147 to 217 days apart and the next after 2026-10-31 is 2027-03-28 (148 days); with a smaller limit, the integration node cannot always book on the next change day through the API under the real clock (ADR-002 Consequences), so state the limit with that in view, or say how the change-day criteria are reached. (2) Which other booking the overlap refusal names when a request overlaps several: an exclusion constraint's 23P01 DETAIL names one conflicting row (hsdd/auto/experiments/time-model-postgres/), so the contract should pick a rule, for example the earliest, and the producer re-reads it.

ADR-002 item 3: the profile serves the account's zone as timeZone, an IANA name (ayu Asia/Jakarta, budi Europe/London), and the web app may use no other zone, so it shows no booking time without it. An optional field under additive-only leaves a consumer nothing to fall back on; the touch should state that the producer always sends it for the built-in accounts, or weigh that in its classification (DEC-007 anticipated this). profile-api@v2's governed_by and body line already read [ADR-001, ADR-002] (DEC-036); the touch need not add them.

ADR-002's affects names simple-login (DEC-035), and the root header and its three embedded summaries now carry ADR-002 under Governed by (simple-login.integration's for the first time); keep those lines when restating the header, or gate C3 errors. A Decisions bullet for ADR-002 can say: instants on the wire and in PostgreSQL, the account's IANA zone, the web app converts and formats, the backend's clock decides.

ADR-002 for the backend's plan: start and end as timestamptz with the half-open overlap rule; an exclusion constraint on tstzrange(start_at, end_at, '[)') with btree_gist is one way to hold AC-5.4, but its 23P01 DETAIL names one row, so the AC-5.3 body needs a re-read (hsdd/auto/experiments/time-model-postgres/); no zone arithmetic in the service; the quarter-hour check on the UTC instant; the injected clock decides started and ended (start equal to now is started); the account data gains timeZone; the gate's tests run with TZ set to a zone that is neither account's nor UTC.

ADR-002 for the web app's plan: one module of pure functions taking the zone as an argument (instant to wall time, a date to [start of date, start of next date), the form's quarter-hour instants, the repeated-hour and other-date marks), tested in isolation on 2027-03-28 (23 hours, 92 slots, no 01:xx) and 2027-10-31 (25 hours, 100 slots, 01:00 to 01:45 twice as BST then GMT) per hsdd/auto/experiments/time-model-intl/; Node.js 24 has no global Temporal, so use Intl or a library on it, or a polyfill; en-GB gives 'Thu 5 Nov', HH:mm with hourCycle h23, GMT and BST (en-US gives GMT+1); Vitest runs with TZ set to a third zone; the browser's clock only picks the Rooms screen's opening date; the overlap message is built from the refusal's instants, not from error.message.

ADR-002 for the integration plan: the browser tests run with the browser's time zone set to a zone that is neither account's nor UTC (for example Asia/Kolkata, +05:30); the change-day tests take the next last Sunday of March and of October after the real clock, never a fixed date (2026-10-25 has passed; the next is 2027-03-28), and booking-api@v1's how-far-ahead limit decides whether that day is bookable through the API; the backend's clock decides 'started', which an end-to-end test cannot set, so the plan says which scripted test covers AC-5.5 and AC-6.2's started case (PRD v2 Success); the strings to assert are ADR-002 item 7's, including '23:00 to Fri 6 Nov 02:00' and '01:30 BST' / '01:30 GMT'.

note: Front matter governed_by: [ADR-001, ADR-002] and the body's Governed by line; every endpoint takes auth-api@v1's bearer token (Interface), and a missing, unknown or expired token is one 401 UNAUTHORIZED case with profile-api@v2's body (G16); there is no logout endpoint; bookings survive the restart that drops tokens (G17). Gate C3 reports no error for ADR-001 or ADR-002 now that the file exists.

governed_by and the Governed by line name both ADRs. Instants in toISOString form only, both directions (Values, G1); the rooms query takes the day as two instants and returns each room's bookings overlapping the half-open range, earliest first (GET /api/rooms, G13); each room carries timeZone and office (RoomWithBookings); [start, end) and touching bookings do not overlap (G3); quarter-hour instants and end after start (G2); started at the clock's reading of start or later, refused for booking and for cancelling (G7, G11); my bookings are those whose end is after the clock, soonest first (G14); the refusal carries the other booking with roomName, start and end as instants in error.conflict (Errors, G6, G18).

(1) A start at most 365 days after the backend's clock (G10, DEC-047): the experiment finds the next London change instant at most 217 days after any clock, so the next change day is always bookable through the API. (2) The refusal names the overlapping booking with the earliest start, re-read by the producer, never a 409 without one (G6, DEC-045); fixture book-overlap-several pins it.

text: booking-api@v1 (S05) takes auth-api@v1's bearer token at all four endpoints until expiresAt and answers a missing, unknown or expired token with profile-api@v2's 401 body (G16); a restart drops tokens and keeps bookings with their ids (G17); there is no logout endpoint. The token guarantee can name booking-api@v1 with no change to auth-api's shapes or fixtures.

booking-api@v1's fixtures (hsdd/contract/fixture/booking-api/, 35, all replay exact) add two fields the current rig (backend/test/replay.ts) cannot replay: clock, the instant the injected clock reads for the whole fixture, tokens included ({{expired-token:u}} is a token whose expiresAt is before clock); and given, bookings to create before the request, directly and with the fixture's UUIDs (some lie before the clock, which POST refuses), starting each fixture from no bookings. The rig also meets DELETE, and a 204 whose fixture body is null while the real response has no body (res.json() throws on an empty body), and a 201 whose id is checked against the schema and must differ from every given id. Each fixture's response validates against the top-level schema; $defs.GetRoomsResponse, GetMyBookingsResponse, PostBookingResponse and DeleteBookingResponse are per endpoint. Booking ids are lower-case UUIDs (gen_random_uuid in PostgreSQL 17), never reused.

booking-api@v1 for the backend's plan: G6 needs a re-read after an exclusion refusal (23P01 DETAIL names one row): the room's overlapping bookings ordered by start, the first one; if none remains because it was cancelled meanwhile, try the insert again, never a 409 without error.conflict and never a 5xx from contention (G5; PRD v2 Success, 20 simultaneous attempts). G1: accept an instant only when new Date(s).toISOString() === s; query values percent-decoded. The limits are instant arithmetic: end - start <= 8 h (G9), start - now <= 8,760 h (G10), started when now >= start (G7). The title counts code points (Ajv's maxLength does, JavaScript's .length does not), needs one non-whitespace character and is stored as sent (G8). The check orders of POST and DELETE are part of the contract (G15); a DELETE id that is not a UUID answers 404. Rooms come back in PRD v2 Rooms' order with ids merapi, bromo, thames, kew; lists sort by start, ties by that order (G13, G14). produced_by is the provisional guess simple-login.backend.4 (DEC-053).

booking-api@v1 for the web's plan: web/src/test/fetchStub.ts matches String(input) against request.path, but the rooms fixtures' paths carry unencoded colons (/api/rooms?from=2026-11-05T00:00:00.000Z&to=...) while URLSearchParams writes %3A, so compare decoded URLs or build the query without encoding (the producer accepts both). A 204 fixture's body is null and new Response(body, { status: 204 }) throws on any body, so the stub answers it with no body. Fixtures carry clock and given, which explain the answer and are never sent. AC-5.3's message is written from error.conflict's roomName, start and end in the user's zone (G18); the codes to branch on are UNAUTHORIZED, VALIDATION_FAILED, BOOKING_TOO_LONG, BOOKING_STARTED, BOOKING_TOO_FAR_AHEAD, BOOKING_CONFLICT, BOOKING_NOT_FOUND (a second tab already cancelled) and BOOKING_NOT_YOURS. The form may offer end times up to start + 8 hours and dates up to 365 days ahead, but the backend's answer decides. Lists arrive sorted; no client sort is needed. consumers names simple-login.web.5 provisionally (DEC-053).

booking-api@v1 for the integration plan: the 365-day horizon keeps the next London clock-change day bookable through the API under the real clock (at most 217 days ahead from any moment, hsdd/auto/experiments/booking-api-fixtures/). PRD v2 Success's 20 simultaneous attempts must give exactly one 201 and nineteen 409 BOOKING_CONFLICT naming the winner (G5, G6); a restart keeps every booking and id but drops tokens, so the test signs in again (G17). The fixtures carry a fixed clock and seeded state that the real service under the real clock cannot reproduce: only the 14 that depend on neither (the eight 400s, the four 401s, cancel-unknown and cancel-malformed-id) can be replayed exactly through the proxy; the stateful criteria are this node's own tests. consumers names simple-login.integration.3 provisionally (DEC-053).
